\chapter{红外光谱}\label{ch:g11:infrared}
=
On a laboratory shelf stands a bottle of colourless liquid whose label
has been torn off. It might be an alcohol, a ketone or an acid: three
families that look exactly alike in a bottle. A drop placed on the
crystal of an infrared spectrometer, two minutes of waiting, and a graph
appears on the screen that answers the question. The bonds of a molecule
vibrate, and each kind of bond absorbs infrared light of its own
frequencies: an infrared spectrum is a list of the bonds present.
=
\begin{recall}
Functional groups and families (\cref{ch:g11:functional-groups})。An
absorption spectrum shows how much light a substance absorbs at each
wavelength (\cref{ch:g11:absorbance})。Hydrogen bonds link \ce{O-H}
groups to neighbouring molecules (\cref{ch:g11:polarity-and-cohesion})。
\end{recall}
=
\section{键的振动}
=
A covalent bond is not rigid: the two atoms vibrate, moving closer and
apart many millions of millions of times per second, like two balls
joined by a spring. A stiffer spring (a double bond rather than a single
one) or lighter balls (a hydrogen atom rather than a carbon atom) vibrate
faster. A bond can absorb infrared light whose frequency matches its own
vibration: infrared light, invisible to the eye, has wavelengths of a few
micrometres to a few tens of micrometres.

\begin{definition}[波数]\label{def:g11:infrared:wavenumber}
=
The \emph{波数}\index{波数} $\sigma$ of a light is the
=
inverse of its wavelength, $\sigma = 1/\lambda$。In infrared
=
spectroscopy it is expressed in \si{cm^{-1}}: the number of wavelengths
=
in one centimetre。A larger wavenumber means a shorter wavelength and a
=
faster vibration.
=
\end{definition}
=
\begin{example}[由波数求波长]\label{ex:g11:infrared:convert}
=
A band at $\sigma = \qty{2000}{cm^{-1}}$ corresponds to
=
$\lambda = 1/2000 = \qty{5.0e-4}{cm} = \qty{5.0}{\micro m}$。Infrared
=
spectra usually run from \qty{4000}{cm^{-1}} (\qty{2.5}{\micro m}) to
=
\qty{500}{cm^{-1}} (\qty{20}{\micro m})。
=
\end{example}
=
\section{读懂红外光谱}
=
\begin{definition}[红外光谱，透射比]\label{def:g11:infrared:spectrum}
=
The \emph{透射比}\index{透射比} $T$ of a sample at a given
=
wavenumber is the percentage of the infrared light that passes through
=
it: \qty{100}{\percent} if nothing is absorbed。The \emph{红外光谱}\index{红外光谱} of a compound is the graph of $T$
=
against the wavenumber, drawn by convention with the wavenumbers
=
decreasing from left to right.
=
\end{definition}
=
\begin{definition}[吸收带，指纹区]\label{def:g11:infrared:band}
=
An \emph{吸收带}\index{吸收带} is a dip of the
=
transmittance: the light of those wavenumbers is absorbed by a bond。Its
=
position tells which bond, its width and its depth complete the
=
picture。Below about \qty{1500}{cm^{-1}}, the spectrum is crowded with
=
bands that depend on the whole molecule: this \emph{指纹区
=
}\index{指纹区} identifies a compound by comparison
=
with a known spectrum, but is hard to read bond by bond.
=
\end{definition}
=
\begin{inthelab}[记录光谱]
=
Most school and university spectrometers now use a small diamond crystal:
=
a drop of liquid, or a few grains of solid pressed by a clamp, is placed
=
on the crystal, and the infrared beam that grazes its surface probes the
=
sample。The crystal is first recorded clean (the “背景”), which
=
plays the part of the blank。The crystal is cleaned with a tissue and a
=
little solvent between two samples.
=
\end{inthelab}
=
